1.note: The author is introducing **Elijah** as a new participant in the story. Your language may have its own way of introducing new participants that you can use in your translation.

1.q: חַי־יְהוָ֞ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָמַ֣דְתִּי לְ⁠פָנָ֔י⁠ו אִם־יִהְיֶ֛ה הַ⁠שָּׁנִ֥ים הָ⁠אֵ֖לֶּה טַ֣ל וּ⁠מָטָ֑ר כִּ֖י אִם־לְ⁠פִ֥י דְבָרִֽ⁠י
1.note: In order to make a solemn proclamation, following the custom of his culture, Elijah is swearing an oath by stating the first part of a condition (“if”) but not the second part (“then”). Use a natural way in your language to express an oath. In a context such as this, it may be natural to express just the first part of the condition as a negative statement. See how you translated the similar expression “if he will kill his servant” in 1:51. Alternate translation: [I swear by Yahweh, the God of Israel, to whose face I stand, that there will not be dew or rain these years except by the mouth of my word]

Here, **face** represents the presence of Yahweh. Elijah is speaking as if he stood in Yahweh’s presence, the way servants stood in the presence of a king, in order to indicate that he serves Yahweh rather than Baal, whom Ahab worshiped. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [whose servant I am]

1.q: אִם־יִהְיֶ֛ה הַ⁠שָּׁנִ֥ים הָ⁠אֵ֖לֶּה טַ֣ל וּ⁠מָטָ֑ר כִּ֖י אִם־לְ⁠פִ֥י דְבָרִֽ⁠י
1.note: If, in your language, it would appear that Elijah was making a statement here and then contradicting it, you could reword this as a positive statement. Alternate translation: [only by the mouth of my word will there be dew or rain these years]

The phrase **by the mouth of my words** represents what Elijah would say by using his mouth to speak words. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [unless I say that there will be]

2.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 6:11. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh spoke a message to him]

3.note: The phrase **for yourself** indicates that this action would be for Elijah’s benefit. The implication is that Elijah should go eastward for his own safety, since he has just angered King Ahab by declaring a drought. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [For your own safety, go from here and travel eastward]

Here, **on the face of** represents being “near” or “beside” the Jordan River. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language, here and in verse 5. Alternate translation: [near the Jordan River]

5.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 9:6. Alternate translation: [And he took action and did … And he took action and dwelled]

6.q: ל֜⁠וֹ לֶ֤חֶם וּ⁠בָשָׂר֙ בַּ⁠בֹּ֔קֶר וְ⁠לֶ֥חֶם וּ⁠בָשָׂ֖ר בָּ⁠עָ֑רֶב
6.note: It might seem that repeating the phrase **bread and meat** would be to express extra information in a way that would not be natural in your language. If so, you could represent the phrase only once in your translation. Alternate translation: [bread and meat to him in the morning and in the evening]

7.note: The author is using the term **days** to refer to time. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [some time]

7.q: וַ⁠יִּיבַ֣שׁ הַ⁠נָּ֑חַל כִּ֛י לֹֽא־הָיָ֥ה גֶ֖שֶׁם בָּ⁠אָֽרֶץ
7.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [that because no rain was in the land, the wadi dried up]

8.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 6:11. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh spoke a message to him]

9.note: To translate the term **Arise** here and the term “arose” in the next verse, how you translated the term “arose” in 1:50. Alternate translation: [Take action]
See how you translated the similar expression in 1:14. Alternate translation: [Listen]

Yahweh does not mean that he has spoken to this widow and **commanded** her to provide food for Elijah. He means that he has commanded for this to happen and will arrange it. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [I have commanded that a woman, a widow, there is to sustain you]

The author is introducing this **woman** as a new participant in the story. Your language may have its own way of introducing new participants that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [a certain woman who is a widow who lives there]

10.note: The expression **and said** introduces a direct quotation. In your translation, use a natural way of introducing direct quotations in your language. It may not be necessary to represent this term explicitly. See how you translated the same expression in 1:28 and comparable contexts.
In a context such as this, a speaker of your language might say “bring” instead of **take** (and similarly in the next verse). Alternate translation: [bring]

Elijah describing the purpose for which he is asking the woman to bring him **a little water**. Use a verb form in your language that will make this clear. Alternate translation: [so that I can drink]

11.note: Elijah, using the courteous hospitality language of this culture, is understating what he is requesting. Use a comparable way of speaking from your own language and culture. If you have already translated the book of 1 Samuel, see how you translated the similar expression in 1 Samuel 28:22. Alternate translation: [a little bit to eat]

By saying **in your hand**, Elijah is specifically requesting the woman’s hospitality, as a guest in a foreign country. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use here in your translation.

12.note: Following the custom of her culture, the woman is swearing an oath by stating the first part of a condition (“if”) but not the second part (“then”). Use a natural way in your language to express an oath. In a context such as this, it may be natural to express just the first part of the condition as a negative statement. See how you translated the similar expression “if he will kill his servant” in 1:51. Alternate translation: [I swear by Yahweh your God that there is not to me a bread-cake] or [I swear by Yahweh your God that I do not have even so much as a bread-cake]
See how you translated the similar expression in 5:5. Alternate translation: [And I am about to gather two sticks]

The widow is using **two sticks** as a common expression of her culture to mean “a few sticks” or “just enough sticks to make a small fire.” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [some sticks]

By **we will die**, the woman does not mean that there is something wrong with the food she has left and it will therefore kill her. She means that she and her son will die of starvation after eating this last meal. Be sure that this is clear in your translation. Alternate translation: [and after that we will have nothing to eat, so we will die of starvation]

13.note: Elijah is not asking the woman to **Come** somewhere. He is using the term **Come** to encourage her to do what he suggests. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Go ahead]
Here, **word** represents what the widow said by using words. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [what you have said]

By **from there**, Elijah means from the flour and oil that the widow has in her containers. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [from that flour and oil]

14.q: כִּ֣י כֹה֩ אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כַּ֤ד הַ⁠קֶּ֨מַח֙ לֹ֣א תִכְלָ֔ה וְ⁠צַפַּ֥חַת הַ⁠שֶּׁ֖מֶן לֹ֣א תֶחְסָ֑ר עַ֠ד י֧וֹם תתן־יְהוָ֛ה גֶּ֖שֶׁם עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הָ⁠אֲדָמָֽה
14.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [For Yahweh, the God of Israel, says that the jar of flour will not finish and the jug of oil will not lack up to the day he gives rain on the face of the ground]
See how you translated the similar expression in 8:40. Alternate translation: [the surface of the ground]

15.note: Here, **word** represents what Elijah said by using words. If it would be clearer in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [what Elijah had told her to do]

The author is speaking of the people who lived with this widow as if they were her **house**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and her family] or [and her son]
The author is using the term **days** to refer to a long period of time. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [for a long time]

16.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 8:53. Alternate translation: [through the agency of]

17.note: The author is using the phrase **And it happened** to introduce a new event in the story. Use a word, phrase, or other method in your language that is natural for introducing a new event.

The author is referring to death in a mild way by using this phrase. Depending on what is helpful in your language, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [he passed away] or [he died]

18.note: The widow is using **What to me and to you** as a common expression of her culture to mean “What do you have against me?” or “What dispute do we have?” If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression from your language that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [What do you have against me, man of God]

The woman is using the question form for emphasis. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [I have done nothing wrong to you, man of God!]

18.q: לִּ֥⁠י & בָּ֧אתָ & לְ⁠הַזְכִּ֥יר אֶת־עֲוֺנִ֖⁠י וּ⁠לְ⁠הָמִ֥ית אֶת־בְּנִֽ⁠י
18.note: The widow is using the question form for emphasis. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [It seems that you came to me to bring my iniquity to remembrance and to kill my son!]

By this expression, the woman could be speaking of: (1) Elijah bringing her **iniquity** to Yahweh’s **remembrance**. Alternate translation: [so that Yahweh would remember my iniquity and punish me by killing my son] or (2) Elijah bringing her **iniquity** to her own **remembrance**. Alternate translation: [to remind me of my iniquity so that I would realize why Yahweh was punishing me by killing my son]

19.note: It might seem that the expression **where he was dwelling there** contains extra information that would not be natural to express in your language. If so, you could shorten it. Alternate translation: [where he was dwelling]

20.q: יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָ֔⁠י הֲ֠⁠גַם עַל־הָ⁠אַלְמָנָ֞ה אֲשֶׁר־אֲנִ֨י מִתְגּוֹרֵ֥ר עִמָּ֛⁠הּ הֲרֵע֖וֹתָ לְ⁠הָמִ֥ית אֶת־בְּנָֽ⁠הּ
20.note: Elijah is using the question form for emphasis. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [Yahweh my God, you should not have harmed even the widow with whom I am sojourning, by killing her son!]

21.note: See the discussion in the introduction to this chapter of the significance of Elijah stretching himself over the child **three times**.

22.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 5:8. Alternate translation: [And Yahweh did what Elijah asked]

24.note: The woman is using **the word of Yahweh** to represent messages from Yahweh, and she is using Elijah’s **mouth** to represent him speaking those messages. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and the messages from Yahweh that you speak]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **truth**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [is true]
